Observe the definition of Module.Injective R M, which only requires the test module X and Y to be in Type v which M lies on.
However, Module.Baer has no other universe issue problem, and it's definitely the definition of injective module in mathematics.
Also, we can see in the file that: Module.Baer implies Module.Injective unconditionally, but the reverse holds only when R is as small as M.

My question is: Which of the following case in real?

  1. Module.Baer and Module.Injective are in fact equivalent, but it was not proven in Mathlib4 yet.
  2. It's strict implication. There exists HUGE R and ₛₘₐₗₗ M such that Module.Injective R M but NOT Module.Baer R M.
  3. It's independent of ZFC.

In each cases, my advise to mathlib4 is:

  1. Modify the proof in that file such that Small R can be dropped.
  2. Change Module.Baer into the main Module.Injective definition and remove the original.
  3. Discussion which we should do next.
I'm guessing (2), will try to prove it now
I also think (2), even if not 100% sure. What usually happens is that universes-related issues only appear when the universe of the module is smaller than the universe of the ring.
To me, the current Module.Injective is the standard definition of injective module. Wikipedia seems to agree with me. So I don't think we should change it.

I think the simplest change is to replace Type v to Type u in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Injective.lean#L62.
This can drop all [Small R] in this file, which is really annoy me for formalize things (and it can be even became the WRONG definition, if [Small R] does not hold with very strange set theoretic constructions).

Changing this to Type u, not the first time to do this, the Module.Flat is also using the universe of ring, not the one of module.
cf. #38546.

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

To me, the current Module.Injective is the standard definition of injective module. Wikipedia seems to agree with me. So I don't think we should change it.

I don't think we should make that the definition, because when you are proving things about injective modules I think you usually don't want to use this definition, which will only work for extending maps in a specific universe. Instead you want to use the more general docs#Module.Baer.extension_property, which extends maps in any universe.

I am not at all sure we should change the definition. The current Module.Injective is equivalent to the property that the module is injective in the category ModuleCat with suitable universe parameters. We have to accept that it is not very well behaved when the ring is not small.

Joël Riou said:

I am not at all sure we should change the definition. The current Module.Injective is equivalent to the property that the module is injective is the category ModuleCat with suitable universe parameters. We have to accept that it is not very well behaved when the ring is not small.

However, in ModuleCat the projective has Small R requirement. We think unify it is also a reasonable way.
if the ring is not Small.{v}, then ModuleCat.{v} R becomes weird anyways (for example, you lose the tensor unit)

I agree with Module.Baer being the injective module in common sense, I discussed with @Andrew Yang earlier about this. We agreed with this.
Module.Injective R M is totally equivalent to CategoryTheory.Injective (ModuleCat.of R M), which I am not very sure neccessary. Then there are only some naming issues left when rearraanging these defs.

#38546 passed CI. This PR make a change as small as possible, make Module.Injective equivalent (but not defeq) to Module.Baer (this change is similar to Module.Flat), and make the dirty universe issue into ModuleCat (I think it's also OK, because ModuleCat.Projective already also have these things)
Any opinion about this? Can we progress the PR?
I think it's time to review and merge this PR.
I agree with the nit in the discussion so that would be a good place to start
Any progress on this PR? @topic
@Kevin Buzzard any opinion or progress?

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

To me, the current Module.Injective is the standard definition of injective module. Wikipedia seems to agree with me. So I don't think we should change it.

For me the question is pathological, I don't care about what is going on in any universe other than Type when I am doing algebra at this level so I have no opinions on this question.

The question seems to boil down to "what if my ring and module are in different universes -- what should the definition of "injective module" be in this setting" and my answer is "I personally don't care". Clearly some other people care but please stop pinging me.

@Sébastien Gouëzel @Joël Riou I have now formalized the counterexample discussed above. I agree that the current definition is a valid definition of an injective object in ModuleCat.{v} R. The point is that, when the ring is not v-small, this can differ from the usual module-theoretic property characterized by Baer's criterion.

injective_zulip.lean

The attached file proves, against the pre-change definition:

theorem main :
    ∃ (R : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Ring R) (M : Type)
      (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M),
      Module.Injective R M ∧ ¬Module.Baer R M

It also proves categorical_counterexample, with CategoryTheory.Injective (ModuleCat.of R M) in place of Module.Injective R M. Both proofs use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no sorry or additional axioms. I checked the file with Lean 4.35.0-rc3 in the Mathlib environment used for this example.

Briefly, the ring is the triangular ring

R = [ Q  F ]
    [ 0  F ]

where F is a characteristic-zero field larger than every Type-small type, and the target module is Q, with action through the upper-left entry. For any Type-small R-module N, the image of the lower-right idempotent is an F-vector space. The cardinality bound forces that image to be zero, so the entire action factors through Q. Extension between these small modules therefore reduces to extension of maps of Q-vector spaces. However, a Q-linear functional F → Q taking 1 to 1 gives a map from the large square-zero ideal that cannot extend to R. Thus the distinction is an actual non-equivalence, rather than just a missing universe-generalization lemma.

Regarding the standard-definition objection: I agree with the usual extension-property definition. The question is which universe supplies the test modules. A definition of injectivity in the small module category does not by itself determine which property the unbundled algebraic name Module.Injective should express. I think it should express the property equivalent to Baer's criterion, while CategoryTheory.Injective continues to express injectivity in the chosen category.

Regarding the categorical correspondence, we already use precisely this distinction for projectivity: Module.Projective R P implies categorical projectivity without [Small R], whereas the converse requires [Small.{v} R]. These are the existing ModuleCat projectivity bridges. Making injectivity follow the same pattern would align it with an existing API convention. It would preserve the categorical notion, with the smallness hypothesis at the converse bridge where it is needed.

There is also the flatness precedent: Module.Flat uses the ring's universe for its defining tests, and supplies application theorems for maps in arbitrary universes. PR #38546 follows the same approach for injectivity: it makes Module.Injective equivalent to Module.Baer without [Small R], and its Module.Injective.extension_property already handles independently chosen source and target universes. So the concern about extending maps in arbitrary universes is addressed by the proposed API.

For these reasons, I would like to move #38546 forward with the existing definition change and bridges, together with clearer documentation of the distinction. The counterexample settles the mathematical non-equivalence; it does not by itself settle the naming choice, but the existing Projective and Flat conventions give a concrete consistency argument for this choice. If there is a remaining objection to this API design, could we identify it explicitly so that it can be addressed and the PR can proceed to review?

Maybe you could also come up with a counterexample of ModuleCat.projective_of_module_projective with Small assumption removed, even example with R commutative?

Personally I think it make sense to rename docs#Module.Baer to Module.Injective and remove the current docs#Module.Injective. That would be essentially parallel to the Module.Projective API design.

Yes, I think it is to change the definition of Module.Injective so that it matches Module.Baer even though it may match CategoryTheory.Injective only when the ring is small. In the next few days, I will have little time to do reviews. Could you add documentation regarding the design choice? [In a future PR, it would be nice to include the counter-example.]

Junyan Xu said:

Maybe you could also come up with a counterexample of ModuleCat.projective_of_module_projective with Small assumption removed, even example with R commutative?

See here for the same commutative example that satisfies all projective, injective, flat when testing module is small but fails all when testing module with the same universe as the ring.

Personally I think it make sense to rename docs#Module.Baer to Module.Injective and remove the current docs#Module.Injective. That would be essentially parallel to the Module.Projective API design.

I don't have particular objection with this change since they are provably equivalent. The reason I change the universe is just that to keep the change as small as possible like docs#Module.Flat, and maybe future PRs are possible to do the docs#Module.Baer → docs#Module.Injective change.
